# Resources {.unnumbered #sec-resources}

This page collects the open resources referenced throughout the module, plus the
practice dataset used in Rubrics 1–4. Everything here is either open-access or
explicitly licensed for reuse — check each source's own licence before adapting it.

## Practice Dataset

The worked example used across [Chapter 1](01-understanding-data.qmd) through
[Chapter 4](04-statistical-modelling.qmd) is **real, open climate data** from the
Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD, Germany's national meteorological service): annual
regional averages of air temperature, precipitation and sunshine duration for five
German Bundesländer (Bayern, Sachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Schleswig-Holstein,
Baden-Württemberg) plus the national "Deutschland" series, covering 1991–2024 (34
years — long enough to see a real, substantial warming trend). Source:
[DWD Climate Data Center, regional averages](https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/regional_averages_DE/annual/),
licensed **CC BY 4.0**. `data/raw/dwd_climate_raw.csv` (the real DWD values, with a
small number of disclosed, deliberately reintroduced formatting issues for Chapter 1's
data-quality exercises) and `data/clean/dwd_climate_clean.csv` (tidy, analysis-ready).
Full column definitions, exact source URLs and a full disclosure of exactly what was
changed for teaching purposes are in `data/README.md` in the project folder. Regenerate
the dataset with `data/generate_climate_dataset.py`.

## By Competency Area

### Understanding and Managing Data {#understanding-and-managing-data}
*(Rubric 1 — [Chapter 1](01-understanding-data.qmd))*

- [Environmental Statistics with R](https://chrisbogner.github.io/environmental_stat/) — Christina Bogner's open lecture notes; the module's overall blueprint. See especially "Data", "Import, Explore, Visualize" and "Tidyverse".
- [`statistik_uebung`](https://chrisbogner.github.io/statistik_uebung/) — statistics exercises (German-language companion material).
- [OpenIntro Modern Statistics — Data](https://openintro-ims.netlify.app/data-hello#sec-variable-types) — variable types and structure.
- [DataCamp — Data Analyst with R career track](https://app.datacamp.com/learn/career-tracks/data-analyst-with-r)
- *Beginner:* [Hands-On Programming with R](https://rstudio-education.github.io/hopr/) — starts from zero R syntax.
- *Going deeper:* [R for Data Science (2e) — Data Tidying](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-tidy)

## About the Blueprint

This module's structure and tone take inspiration from Christina Bogner's
[*Environmental Statistics*](https://chrisbogner.github.io/environmental_stat/)
lecture notes (Bookdown, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) — numbered chapters building from data
basics through modelling, worked exercises throughout and an appendix of further
resources. This module is built in **Quarto** rather than Bookdown (Quarto is
Bookdown/R Markdown's direct successor, same underlying idea, actively developed),
which is why the two sites look different, but the pedagogical shape is deliberately
close.
